title: Simple Bench
description: A simple bench is three seat boards over a four-leg frame with aprons and one long stretcher, built entirely from straight cuts and butt joints. The seat sits 18 inches high, a standard sitting height, and the stretcher keeps the legs from splaying when someone sits down hard. It works as an entry bench, a garden bench indoors, or extra seating at a table, and it is the first project a beginner should build after the practice table.

title: Stool
description: A three-legged stool has a round oak seat and three legs splayed outward, which makes it stable on uneven floors where a four-legged stool would rock. The legs angle about 10 degrees from vertical and are joined with stretchers, called rungs, near the floor, which also give feet a rest. It is a counter-height stool at 24 inches, suited to a kitchen counter or a workbench, and its round seat is cut with a jigsaw or a router circle jig.

The pegs angle slightly upward and are glued and screwed from behind the board, so no screw head shows on the face and no peg can pull straight out under a heavy winter coat. It suits an entry, a mudroom, or a bedroom door wall, and the board can be shaped with a rounded top edge for a finished profile.
